A plugin channel or insert can be set to 'Run in a separate process' (a checkbox in its settings, under the plugin's name; undoable and saved in the .lime). LimeShot then starts a copy of itself as a plugin bridge for it and talks to it over two Unix-socket connections (control calls, and one request/reply per audio block with a 500 ms limit). If the bridge crashes, hangs or quits, the slot goes silent, LimeShot shows 'X (place) crashed; it is silent until reloaded', and the plugin's settings show 'The plugin crashed' with a Reload button, which starts it again with the state last saved in the project. Switching keeps the plugin's sound (its state moves along) and reopens its window. Differs from FL: a bridged plugin's own editor is not shown (its parameters are listed instead); macOS and Linux only; plugins not set to run separately still run inside LimeShot.
